prerequisites: Mathematics: algebraic equations, exponential and trigonometric functions, limits, derivatives and integrals.
Physics: principles of mechanics, physical quantities and units of measure.

Thermodynamics: principles of thermodynamics, the concept of "system" (open and closed), equations of state, state functions and thermodynamic properties of fluids, specific heat, thermodynamic diagrams (T-s, h-s, p-v), thermodynamic cycles, mass and energy balances
Fluid dynamics: concept of "control volume" (open system), characteristics of one-dimensional stationary flows, balance of matter and energy applied to the control volume.
Strong correlation with the course of Fluid Machinery.

learning_outcomes.text: To acquire the fundamental knowledge and ability to interpret the structural and functional characteristics of thermal power plants based on steam and gas turbines, their operating principles, performance, environmental implications, and technological evolution.

To provide capacity, starting from the knowledge gained, to represent, analyze and evaluate the thermodynamic cycles and function schemes of steam and gas turbine plants, to set and solve mass and energy balances of the system and its fundamental components, and to evaluate the performance characteristics.

To acquire the ability to recognize plant components and system solutions of different sizes, types, and configurations, to estimate the orders of magnitude of the different performance indices in relation to these characteristics, and to perform comparative analysis and assessment in qualitative and quantitative terms.

To acquire the ability to represent, describe, summarize and comment, in graphical, written, and oral form, the thermodynamic cycles, the physical processes, the functional schemes, the system configurations, the technological solutions, and the formulation of energy balances of steam and gas turbine plants and their basic components.

To acquire the ability to use the fundamental knowledge and methods of analysis learned for the study of the subject at a higher level, with particular reference to the study of more complex and efficient energy systems, the most advanced technologies in developing, related subjects concerning, in particular, the rational use of energy and the environmental impact of energy systems.

syllabus_topics: General Principles of analysis and evaluation of energy systems and their performance.
Energy equation for internal and external combustion systems.
Analysis of thermodynamic power cycles in the ideal, limit and real conditions.
Efficiency of a thermal power plant.
Utilization factor of a power plant, cost of energy produced.
Efficiency and specific work (steam turbine plants).
Methods to increase efficiency (steam turbine plants).
System configuration schemes, and component characteristics (steam turbine plants).
Elementary circuit and thermodynamic cycle (gas turbine plants).
Efficiency and specific work of ideal, limit and real cycles (gas turbine plants).
Energy balance of gas turbine plants.
Current technologies of industrial and aero-derivative gas turbines.
Gas-steam combined cycle power plants; guiding principles and simplified schemes.
Energy balance and efficiency of combined cycles.
Plant for combined production of heat and power (CHP).
Visit to a thermal power plant.
teaching_methods: Visit to a thermal power plant
assessment_rules: The examination consists of a written test and an oral exam. Students who achieve at least 18/30 in both partial written intermediate evaluation tests are exempted from the official written test for the June-July session. The written test and intermediate assessment tests are approved if all exercises are carried out successfully; written tests are valid only for the session concerned and expire with a negative oral examination. The overall assessment usually gives prevalence to the result of the oral exam.
